description: A coalition of EU member states, regional energy regulators, and independent cybersecurity auditors jointly declare the formation of the Systemic Grid Integrity Network (SGIN), a new cross-border coordination body to monitor, stress-test, and enforce resilience standards on AI-managed power grid systems. The initiative emerges in direct response to persistent instability concerns and the voluntary pause in automation upgrades, formalizing information sharing and mandating real-time anomaly reporting. While not a formal EU measure, it gains legitimacy through participation by Germany, France, the Nordics, and ENTSO-E, creating de facto standards that outpace supranational action.

A joint research consortium led by Swiss and German institutes announces a breakthrough in energy-efficient AI training, demonstrating a novel sparse activation architecture that reduces compute requirements for models at the current frontier by 40% without sacrificing performance. The method is open-sourced, and early replications confirm the results. This lowers the barrier to entry for non-frontier actors and redistributes strategic advantage toward algorithmic innovation rather than raw compute monopolies, potentially accelerating openweight capability growth in the next turn.
